title: Unapproved VM-Read Access to LSASS
exclusions: Detects complete Microsoft Sysmon ProcessAccess event 10 records targeting the real Windows System32 `lsass.exe` where the requested GrantedAccess mask includes `PROCESS_VM_READ` (0x0010) and no exact, in-window approval exists for host, normalized source image, source user, and normalized access mask. It reports that a process opened/requested a handle with memory-read rights; it does not prove ReadProcessMemory was called, bytes were read, credentials were present or extracted, a dump file was created, the request succeeded beyond the observed handle event, or credential theft occurred. It does not attest LSA protection/RunAsPPL configuration or runtime protected-process level, Credential Guard, SSP/package integrity, handle duplication without a qualifying event, kernel/driver access, snapshots/minidumps not represented by event 10, offline dumps, renamed/copy LSASS processes outside the qualified path, or systems/configurations that exclude the event. Event 10 can be noisy and legitimate security, identity, backup, diagnostic, and Windows components can request these rights. This documentation review did not validate Sysmon, access-mask conversion, approvals, PPL posture, SPL, or response in production.
evidence: Retain covered-host/OS inventory; Sysmon binary version/hash/signature, effective XML/schema/hash, ProcessAccess include rules, event 16 configuration changes, event 4 service state, event 255 errors, and source/field health; raw event 10 XML; `windows_lsass_vmread_approvals.csv` revision; approved product/version/signer/hash evidence; separate LSA protection policy/runtime attestation and CodeIntegrity 3033/3063 results; saved search `windows_unapproved_lsass_vmread_access` definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and rows; process/file/module/network/EDR correlation; alert actions; incident dispositions; and dated 0x0010, 0x1010, full-access, no-read-bit, approved, expired, wrong-user, malformed-mask, alternate-target, duplicate, and late-arrival tests. Preserve host/time, source/target GUID/PID/image/user, raw/decimal mask, CallTrace, record ID, approval/revision, raw reference, and conclusion. Documentation review generated no runtime evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, ingest one Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon event 10 with `Computer=lsass-lab-01`, `EventRecordID=10001`, `SourceProcessGUID={11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111}`, `SourceProcessId=4242`, `SourceImage=C:\\Lab\\reader.exe`, `SourceUser=LAB\\analyst`, `TargetProcessGUID={22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222}`, `TargetProcessId=688`, `TargetImage=C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe`, `GrantedAccess=0x1010`, and a fixed CallTrace; provide no approval. Expect exactly one row with `granted_access_decimal=4112`, `vm_read_requested=1`, normalized identities, and `approval_state=unapproved`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: For the fixture, publish an exact normalized approval row for `lsass-lab-01,c:\\lab\\reader.exe,lab\\analyst,0x1010` with inclusive start at or before event time and exclusive end after it plus nonempty approval ID, owner, approver, product version/hash, and revision; expect zero alert rows while preserving the approved base event separately. Also expect zero rows for GrantedAccess 0x1000 (query-limited only), malformed `GrantedAccess`, Sysmon event 1, a TargetImage outside `\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe`, wrong provider/channel, missing process GUID/record ID, and a duplicate EventRecordID. Expired, future, wrong-host/image/user/mask approval must alert.

dataSources: Primary source: Microsoft Sysmon provider `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon`, channel `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, ProcessAccess event 10, collected with Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709). Required fields: `UtcTime`, `SourceProcessGUID`, `SourceProcessId`, `SourceThreadId`, `SourceImage`, `SourceUser`, `TargetProcessGUID`, `TargetProcessId`, `TargetImage`, `TargetUser`, `GrantedAccess`, `CallTrace`, event/provider/channel/version, host/computer, EventRecordID/RecordNumber, event time, and index time; verify exact casing/template on every Sysmon/schema/add-on version. Effective Sysmon XML must include access to System32 lsass. Governance source: exact time-bounded approvals keyed by normalized host, source image, source user, and access-mask string. Separate source: authoritative LSA protection policy/runtime attestation; it is not inferred from event 10.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709) for Sysmon Operational collection, field knowledge, and optional CIM mapping. A deployment-owned credential-access security app must provide Sysmon configuration/source health, exact LSASS access approvals, PPL posture integration, saved search, fixtures, dashboard, and response runbook.
spl:
index=windows source IN ("WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational","XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational") sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog","XmlWinEventLog") EventCode=10 earliest=-15m@m latest=@m
| eval sample_host=lower(coalesce(Computer,dest,host)), event_record_id=coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber), provider=coalesce(Provider_Name,ProviderName), source_process_guid=lower(coalesce(SourceProcessGUID,SourceProcessGuid)), target_process_guid=lower(coalesce(TargetProcessGUID,TargetProcessGuid)), source_image=lower(trim(SourceImage)), source_user=lower(trim(SourceUser)), target_image=lower(trim(TargetImage)), granted_access=lower(trim(GrantedAccess)), granted_access_decimal=tonumber(replace(lower(trim(GrantedAccess)),"^0x",""),16)
| where provider="Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" AND len(sample_host)>0 AND len(event_record_id)>0 AND len(source_process_guid)>0 AND len(target_process_guid)>0 AND len(source_image)>0 AND len(source_user)>0 AND len(target_image)>0 AND isnotnull(granted_access_decimal)
| where like(target_image,"%\\windows\\system32\\lsass.exe") AND bit_and(granted_access_decimal,16)=16
| dedup sample_host source event_record_id
| eval vm_read_requested=1
| lookup windows_lsass_vmread_approvals.csv sample_host source_image source_user granted_access OUTPUTNEW approved_start_epoch approved_end_epoch approval_id approval_owner approver approved_product_version approved_source_hash approval_revision
| eval approval_complete=if(len(approval_id)>0 AND len(approval_owner)>0 AND len(approver)>0 AND len(approved_product_version)>0 AND len(approved_source_hash)>0 AND len(approval_revision)>0 AND isnotnull(tonumber(approved_start_epoch)) AND isnotnull(tonumber(approved_end_epoch)),1,0), approval_state=if(approval_complete=1 AND _time>=tonumber(approved_start_epoch) AND _time<tonumber(approved_end_epoch),"approved","unapproved")
| where approval_state="unapproved"
| table _time _indextime sample_host EventCode event_record_id provider source sourcetype UtcTime source_process_guid SourceProcessId SourceThreadId source_image source_user target_process_guid TargetProcessId target_image TargetUser granted_access granted_access_decimal vm_read_requested CallTrace approval_state approval_id approval_owner approver approved_product_version approved_source_hash approval_revision
| sort 0 - _time sample_host event_record_id
description: Returns one event-grain row for each complete, deduplicated Sysmon event 10 in which a process opens System32 LSASS with a GrantedAccess mask containing the documented `PROCESS_VM_READ` bit and lacks an exact valid approval for host, source image, source user, and mask at event time. It reports requested handle rights, not a completed memory read or credential dump.
value: Memory-read access to LSASS is a prerequisite used by many credential-dumping workflows and is also used by legitimate security software. Exact product-bound reconciliation gives responders an early signal without trusting process names alone, while preserving process GUID, access mask, and call trace for rapid correlation with dump files, suspicious execution, and identity risk.
implementation: Deploy and attest Sysmon with a narrowly tested ProcessAccess include for the real System32 LSASS target, collect event 10 through Splunk Add-on for Sysmon, and prove all fields/access-mask conversion. Publish exact source-image/user/mask approvals backed by product version and binary hash, with separate source/config health and separate RunAsPPL posture collection. Save the SPL as `windows_unapproved_lsass_vmread_access`, run every five minutes over a measured 15-minute arrival window, and investigate every row through ProcessGuid, binary trust, dump/file, module, network, endpoint, and identity evidence.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — LSASS Access Governance`: show covered hosts with missing Sysmon, ProcessAccess rule/config drift, service stop/error, malformed masks, or stale PPL posture first; then unapproved VM_READ events by source image/user, mask, host, call-trace family, and time, approval-match rate, product version/hash mismatch, repeat source, and disposition. Drill down to raw event 10, exact approval, Sysmon event 1 ProcessGuid lineage, file hash/signature/prevalence, dump/file events, EDR/module/network data, LSA protection attestation, CodeIntegrity 3033/3063, and incident. Never label a row “credentials dumped” without outcome evidence.
schema: Microsoft Sysmon ProcessAccess event 10 plus Windows process access-right semantics and exact source approvals
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable to the primary detector. Splunk Add-on for Sysmon may map Endpoint data, but Endpoint.Processes describes process creation and does not guarantee ProcessAccess source/target GUIDs, GrantedAccess, CallTrace, record identity, or approval interval. A post-detection summary can support reporting only after raw parity; it cannot establish memory-read outcome or PPL state.

knownFalsePositives:
Legitimate components can open LSASS with memory-read rights. Authorization must be tied to exact deployed software evidence, not a familiar process name.

1. **EDR/antimalware credential-theft protection** — Security sensors may inspect or instrument LSASS. Verify product/tenant policy, exact version, signed binary and cryptographic hash, installation path/ACL, sensor health, source ProcessGuid lineage, expected mask/call trace, owner, and vendor behavior. A path containing “Defender” or a vendor name is not enough.

2. **Identity, SSO, credential, or password-management agent** — Authentication and credential-management software may interact with LSASS. Confirm supported integration design, installed module/service, source binary hash/signature, service account, product version, exact mask, change record, and identity owner.

3. **Backup, snapshot, forensic, or diagnostic tooling** — Approved tools may inspect processes during support or evidence acquisition. Require case/ticket, named host/operator, exact binary/hash/mask, start/exclusive expiry, evidence-handling plan, and output destination; verify whether full memory collection was intended.

4. **Windows compatibility, telemetry, or troubleshooting component** — Signed Microsoft components can request process information or memory access. Validate exact binary catalog/hash/version, Windows build/KB, parent/service context, mask, CallTrace, and support trace. Never suppress all Microsoft-signed images.

5. **Crash reporting or application compatibility assessment** — Enterprise diagnostics may touch LSASS during broad process enumeration. Verify tool mode, scope, owner, source hash, command line, whether VM_READ was required, and approved collection policy; narrow the tool rather than granting indefinite access.

6. **Security validation, red-team, or purple-team exercise** — Authorized operators may test credential-dumping prevention. Require exercise ID, isolated/approved hosts/accounts, exact tool hash and source image, fixed times, expected event/dump/prevention outcome, approver, identity-response coordination, and cleanup.

7. **Sysmon configuration or version change** — Broader ProcessAccess filters, Sysmon updates, or changed access reporting can surface previously excluded benign processes. Compare event 16, effective XML/hash/schema, version, event volume, and field semantics before adding approvals.

8. **Source binary upgrade with stable path** — An approved product can update in place while retaining image path and mask. The lookup requires product version/hash evidence; verify signer/catalog, deployment job, release, and behavior, then create a new bounded approval rather than accepting the path forever.

9. **Mask parsing or field defect** — Missing `0x`, malformed hex, decimal rendering, extraction truncation, or unexpected casing can cause incorrect conversion or approval mismatch. The SPL rejects non-hex conversion, but analysts must compare raw XML, `tonumber(...,16)`, computed decimal, Sysmon schema, and add-on extraction.

10. **Duplicate WEC/local forwarding or replay** — One event may arrive through multiple routes or queue recovery. Verify host/source/EventRecordID, UtcTime, `_indextime`, collector subscriptions, source health, and durable checkpoint before classifying repeats as multiple access operations.

**Safe suppression:** populate `windows_lsass_vmread_approvals.csv` before deployment with exact lowercase `sample_host,source_image,source_user,granted_access`, inclusive `approved_start_epoch`, exclusive `approved_end_epoch`, `approval_id`, `approval_owner`, `approver`, `approved_product_version`, cryptographic `approved_source_hash`, and immutable `approval_revision`. Reject wildcard hosts/users/images, basename-only paths, signer/vendor-wide rules, mask ranges, omitted version/hash, open-ended windows, and retroactive approvals. At alert time, independently correlate the source ProcessGuid to event 1 or EDR and require observed binary hash/version to equal approval evidence before disposition. Preserve approved base events. Never suppress Sysmon/PPL/source health, malformed masks, product-hash mismatch, dump-file creation, or suspicious post-access behavior.
detectionType: TTP-aligned governed process-access event with VM_READ right
hardware: Supported Windows clients and servers with Microsoft Sysmon installed, a qualified ProcessAccess rule that records opens of the genuine System32 LSASS process, and centrally retained Operational events. Systems without event 10 coverage, nonstandard Windows directories not matched after qualification, or unsupported Sysmon schemas are outside coverage.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft Sysmon ProcessAccess, Windows process-right/ReadProcessMemory, and LSA protection documentation; current MITRE ATT&CK LSASS Memory and process-access strategy; and Splunk Add-on for Sysmon listing; Sysmon XML, fields, bit-mask SPL, approvals, PPL separation, fixtures, outcome correlation, alerting, dashboard, and response were specified but not executed or Windows/LSASS/Sysmon/Splunk-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: Sysmon ProcessAccess can be high volume if configured broadly. The detector scans 15 minutes of event 10, converts hexadecimal masks, performs one bit test, deduplicates records, and joins one exact lookup. Use a tested LSASS-target include and base source/event constraints, but do not collection-filter legitimate-looking source names.
sources: Sysmon configuration, service, error, and source health
separate LSA protection posture and CodeIntegrity evidence
optional process, file/dump, module, network, EDR, and identity telemetry

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and claim boundary

Assign Windows identity/LSA, endpoint engineering, security-product, security operations, Splunk data/content, privacy, change, and incident owners. Inventory stable host identity, OS/build/SystemRoot, LSASS protection policy/runtime, Credential Guard where applicable, Sysmon binary/version/hash/signature, XML/schema/hash, ProcessAccess scope, channel capacity, WEC/forwarder routes, Splunk add-on, approval owner, and retirement time.

Microsoft states Sysmon event 10 reports when one process opens another and is often followed by queries or address-space reads/writes; it can be noisy. Microsoft defines PROCESS_VM_READ as 0x0010 and requires it for ReadProcessMemory. The SPL tests that bit in the requested GrantedAccess integer. Event 10 does not report a ReadProcessMemory call, bytes returned, credentials, or success of credential extraction, so alert text must say “VM_READ access requested/observed,” not “LSASS dumped.”

This UC does not measure memory protection status. RunAsPPL/LSA protection is a preventive posture with separate policy/runtime and CodeIntegrity evidence. A protected LSASS can still generate access attempts, and one event cannot establish whether protection blocked subsequent behavior. Keep posture and activity panels separate.

## Step 1 — Configure and attest Sysmon ProcessAccess

Deploy current Microsoft-signed Sysmon and preserve binary version/hash/signature. Use a versioned XML whose ProcessAccess include matches the real `C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe` target (and qualified alternate SystemRoot drives) while retaining all source images. Microsoft advises filtering expected accesses because event 10 can be voluminous, but do not exclude EDR, Windows, or signed sources at collection; those identities require central approval and can be abused.

Validate XML with `sysmon64 -c config.xml`, record schema with `sysmon64 -s`, and preserve effective config/hash. Monitor event 16 configuration changes, event 4 service state, event 255 errors, service/binary integrity, and a controlled heartbeat. Build `windows_sysmon_lsass_coverage_health` that compares covered hosts with expected Sysmon/config hash, ProcessAccess rule, fresh channel ingestion, and field/mask tests. Missing telemetry is unknown coverage, not safe LSASS.

If built-in Sysmon is used on newer Windows rather than Sysinternals packaging, qualify provider name, event template, configuration path/tooling, and add-on support separately. Do not assume feature parity from the shared name.

## Step 2 — Collect and verify event fields

Use Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709). Configure the Universal Forwarder or WEC to collect `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational` into deployment-local `index=windows`; the index is not a Splunk default. Qualify `sourcetype=WinEventLog` with classic source and `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` with XML source, then retain only supported source/type pairs in production.

On disposable systems for every OS/Sysmon/schema/add-on/rendering combination, generate a benign handle open from a signed lab utility without reading or writing memory. Export raw event 10 XML and verify UtcTime, SourceProcessGUID, SourceProcessId, SourceThreadId, SourceImage, SourceUser, TargetProcessGUID, TargetProcessId, TargetImage, TargetUser, GrantedAccess, CallTrace, Computer, provider/channel/version, EventRecordID or RecordNumber, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Confirm exact GUID capitalization and aliases.

Test masks 0x1000 (query-limited only), 0x0010 (VM_READ only where possible), 0x1010 (query-limited plus read), and a mask containing multiple rights. Independently convert hex to decimal and assert `bit_and(decimal,16)=16` only when the read bit is set. Confirm malformed/decimal/unprefixed representations are rejected or explicitly adapted after evidence. Do not copy internet mask lists without verifying Windows rights.

Measure p99 event/index delay, duplicate routes, event loss, CallTrace size, and mask distributions. Report null GUID/user/mask, target path drift, nonhex values, record gaps, future UtcTime, config changes, and channel overwrite separately.

## Step 3 — Govern exact legitimate access

Publish `windows_lsass_vmread_approvals.csv` from security-product/identity/change governance. Normalize lowercase host, full source image path, source user, and lowercase canonical `0x...` mask. Include inclusive start, exclusive end, approval ID, owner, approver, exact product version, cryptographic source binary hash, immutable revision, expected signer/catalog, service/package ID, CallTrace family where stable, reason, and test date.

Validate start < end, bounded duration, no wildcard host/user/path, no basename or vendor/signer-wide entry, exact mask, complete version/hash, unique key/window, UTC conversion, approval predating deployment, and lookup checksum/signature. Because event 10 does not include source hash, the lookup controls candidate routing; responders or an enrichment pipeline must correlate SourceProcessGUID to Sysmon event 1/EDR and compare the observed binary hash/version before closing as approved. A path-only match is not a final trust decision.

Review approvals after every EDR, identity agent, Windows, backup, diagnostic, or Sysmon change. A stable path with changed binary must fail the disposition check and receive a new evidence-backed approval.

## Step 4 — Create and understand the SPL

Save as `windows_unapproved_lsass_vmread_access`. Schedule every five minutes with `earliest=-15m@m latest=@m` only after measured p99 delay. Use a durable checkpoint keyed on sample_host, source, event_record_id, source_process_guid, target_process_guid, granted_access, and event time so overlap catches late events without duplicate pages.

The base search fixes `index=windows`, Sysmon Operational sources/renderings, and event 10. The first eval normalizes host, aliases, source/target GUIDs, image/user, target, and mask; it strips only a leading `0x` and passes the remaining text to `tonumber(...,16)`. The completeness guard rejects missing identity and conversion failures.

The target condition requires a path ending `\windows\system32\lsass.exe`; qualify non-C drive and localized deployment behavior in fixtures. The bitwise condition tests decimal bit 16 (hex 0x0010), independent of other granted bits. `dedup` removes one host/source/record repeat per dispatch. Exact lookup then validates governance metadata and inclusive-start/exclusive-end and returns unapproved events.

Preserve a companion report of approved candidate matches and the observed hash/version verification result. Keep raw GrantedAccess and decimal output. Do not reduce the alert to a hard-coded list such as 0x1010/0x143a because rights can be combined differently, and tool attribution from one mask is unsupported.

## Step 5 — LSA protection and CIM separation

Collect LSA protection posture from accountable policy and runtime attestation. Microsoft documents RunAsPPL values and deployment methods, version-dependent defaults, and CodeIntegrity Operational events 3033/3063 for plug-ins/drivers that fail protected-LSA requirements. Store OS build, policy source, RunAsPPL mode, UEFI lock status where applicable, boot/restart evidence, runtime verification method, attestation time, and owner. A registry value alone may not prove current runtime state, especially with UEFI/version behavior.

Do not infer PPL from event 10 volume or absence. Dashboard posture can prioritize an unapproved access on a host whose protection is absent/stale, but the event result remains valid independently. Credential Guard is also separate and does not remove all LSASS secrets or access risk.

Keep CIM empty for the primary detector. Endpoint.Processes can provide source process creation context, but it does not represent a process-handle open. Use SourceProcessGUID to correlate Sysmon event 1 command line, parent, hashes, signer, integrity, logon/session, and termination; PID-only joins are unsafe because reuse occurs.

## Step 6 — Correlate outcome evidence

Search for dump/file creation and execution behavior through qualified Sysmon 1/7/11/23/26, Windows Error Reporting, EDR memory/dump alerts, module loads, file hashes/signatures, command/script logs, and network activity. MITRE DET0363 describes a sequence that combines abnormal LSASS access with later dump/file/registry behavior; this SPL detects only the access stage.

Inspect SourceProcessGUID lineage, binary trust and prevalence, parent/service, user/logon privileges, SeDebugPrivilege context where available, CallTrace modules, and target LSASS identity. Determine whether the source is a known sensor, diagnostic, signed but unexpected component, unsigned binary, LOLBin, or injected process. A suspicious CallTrace can strengthen priority but must be versioned/baselined; do not use an unreviewed substring as proof.

If a dump exists, preserve its path/hash/ACL/timestamps and handle as credential material under restricted evidence procedure. Review affected logon sessions and identity risk; do not automatically reset every domain credential from an access event without establishing scope and following incident authority.

## Step 7 — Validate detection and controls

Create fixed-time fixtures for 0x0010, 0x1010, combined/full masks, uppercase hex, no `0x`, decimal text, invalid hex, zero, 0x1000, wrong target path, spoofed `C:\Temp\lsass.exe`, null SourceUser/GUID/record ID, classic/XML aliases, wrong provider/channel/source/type, duplicate route, and late arrival. Assert decimal, bit result, one-row grain, and nonclaims.

Test approval exactly at inclusive start, one second before end, exactly at exclusive end, future/expired, wrong host/path/user/mask, path case, missing version/hash/owner, duplicate keys, stale bundle, and wildcard rejection. Exactly-at-end must alert. Test observed source hash/version mismatch even when the lookup key matches; disposition must remain unresolved/high priority.

On a disposable host, use a minimal internally reviewed utility to request only documented rights and close the handle. Do not invoke Mimikatz, ProcDump against production LSASS, create real credential dumps, disable PPL/Credential Guard, or weaken Sysmon/EDR. If full dump-chain validation is required, perform it in an isolated synthetic-credential lab under identity/IR approval.

Load-test diagnostic/EDR bursts, event 10 volume, Sysmon CPU/channel size, WEC fan-in, CallTrace size, mask conversion, lookup bundles, scheduler overlap, correlation cost, RBAC, and 180-day retention. Verify source/config/PPL health alerts continue during exceptions.

## Step 8 — Alert, investigate, and respond

Alert title: `Unapproved VM_READ access to LSASS on <host>`. Include UTC event/index time, host, source/target ProcessGUID/PID/image/user, raw/decimal mask, CallTrace, provider/source/record ID, approval/revision, observed versus approved source hash/version, Sysmon health/config hash, PPL posture age/state, and raw/correlation links.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify raw event 10, target is genuine System32 LSASS, mask conversion/read bit, GUIDs, record identity, source/config health, and duplicate routes.
2. Re-evaluate exact approval, lookup revision/window, product owner, version/hash evidence, and actual source binary hash/signature via ProcessGuid/event 1 or EDR.
3. Reconstruct source process command/parent/session/integrity/service, binary origin/prevalence, CallTrace, and nearby process injection/tampering.
4. Verify LSA protection/Credential Guard posture separately at event time and review CodeIntegrity/endpoint prevention evidence.
5. Search for dump/minidump/snapshot/file, registry, module, script, network, archive, exfiltration, and cleanup behavior.
6. Determine affected logon sessions/accounts and whether credential material could have been exposed; involve identity response under policy.
7. Validate security/identity/diagnostic/backup/test workflows against exact host/user/path/mask/hash/version/time.
8. If unauthorized, preserve volatile and file evidence and follow accountable endpoint/identity containment and credential-response procedures.
9. Revalidate binary/product integrity, Sysmon/PPL posture, no dump/exfiltration, and no continued accesses before closure.

Do not automatically kill the source, terminate LSASS, reboot/isolate the host, delete a dump, disable an account, rotate all credentials, or alter PPL/security software from one event. LSASS termination can restart or destabilize the system, and abrupt actions can destroy evidence.

## Step 9 — Troubleshooting and maintenance

- **No event 10:** verify Sysmon service/version/config hash, ProcessAccess include, target path, channel, WEC/input, queues, source/type/index/RBAC, and event 16/255.
- **Excess volume:** target LSASS in Sysmon XML and govern exact sources centrally; do not collection-exclude vendors or masks that might hide abuse.
- **Mask conversion null:** inspect raw XML/type/casing; confirm hexadecimal format and add-on extraction before adapting parser.
- **Expected source alerts:** verify actual hash/version/signer and exact mask/user, then create a bounded approval; never add basename/vendor wildcard.
- **No dump evidence:** event 10 is still a handle-access signal; classify outcome unknown after checking telemetry health rather than claiming prevention.
- **PPL panel disagrees:** inspect OS build, policy source, UEFI lock, restart/runtime attestation, and freshness. Event 10 cannot resolve the disagreement.
- **Duplicate alerts:** compare source/record IDs, WEC routes, replay, checkpoint, and overlap; throttle on full event identity, not source image alone.
- **CIM process search differs:** expected; process creation and process access are different grains.

Review host/SystemRoot, Sysmon version/XML/schema/config hash, health, fields/mask format, delay window, approvals and source hashes, PPL/Credential Guard posture, CodeIntegrity, outcome correlation, ATT&CK version, RBAC/retention, dashboard, runbook, and exceptions quarterly and after Windows, LSA, EDR/identity/backup products, Sysmon, WEC/forwarder, add-on, lookup, or Splunk changes. Keep `status=draft` until Windows/identity, Sysmon, security-product, and Splunk owners execute and sign the matrix.
grandmaExplanation: Windows keeps sign-in secrets in a protected process. We flag programs that ask for permission to read that process's memory unless the exact security tool and access were approved, but we still need other evidence before saying any password was stolen.
